---
title: "Factorial ANOVA Decision Tool"
full-width: true
toc: false
---

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## How to use this tool

1. Select the **design type** (Mixed, Between-Between, or Within-Within ANOVA).
2. Indicate whether the **interaction was significant** in your SPSS output.
3. If the interaction was not significant, select the significance status of each **main effect**.
4. Specify the **number of levels** for each factor if you want tailored pairwise comparison guidance.
5. Click **Show decision path** to generate your interpretation steps and APA-style reporting examples.

This tool is companion to [Appendix @sec-appendix-spss-factorial-anova] (SPSS Tutorial: Factorial ANOVA).
:::

```{=html}
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
  <style>
    :root {
      --bg: #f6f8fb;
      --panel: #ffffff;
      --text: #1f2937;
      --muted: #6b7280;
      --line: #dbe3ee;
      --accent: #2563eb;
      --accent-soft: #dbeafe;
      --good: #166534;
      --good-bg: #dcfce7;
      --warn: #92400e;
      --warn-bg: #fef3c7;
      --shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.08);
      --radius: 18px;
    }

    .fadt-wrap * { box-sizing: border-box; }

    .fadt-wrap {
      font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
      color: var(--text);
      line-height: 1.5;
      margin: 0 0 24px 0;
    }

    .fadt-grid {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: 320px 1fr;
      gap: 20px;
      align-items: start;
    }

    @media (max-width: 860px) {
      .fadt-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
    }

    .fadt-card {
      background: var(--panel);
      border: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-radius: var(--radius);
      box-shadow: var(--shadow);
      padding: 20px;
    }

    .fadt-section-title {
      margin: 0 0 12px;
      font-size: 1.05rem;
      font-weight: 700;
    }

    .fadt-wrap label {
      display: block;
      margin: 14px 0 5px;
      font-weight: 700;
      font-size: 0.9rem;
    }

    .fadt-wrap select {
      width: 100%;
      padding: 10px 12px;
      border-radius: 10px;
      border: 1px solid #cbd5e1;
      font-size: 0.95rem;
      background: #fff;
    }

    .fadt-btn-row { display: flex; gap: 10px; margin-top: 16px; }

    .fadt-wrap button {
      flex: 1;
      padding: 11px 14px;
      border-radius: 10px;
      border: none;
      font-size: 0.95rem;
      font-weight: 700;
      cursor: pointer;
      transition: opacity 0.15s, transform 0.1s;
    }
    .fadt-wrap button:hover { opacity: 0.9; }
    .fadt-wrap button:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

    .fadt-run-btn  { background: var(--accent); color: #fff; }
    .fadt-reset-btn { background: #475569; color: #fff; }

    .fadt-helper {
      margin-top: 10px;
      font-size: 0.86rem;
      color: var(--muted);
    }

    .fadt-output { display: grid; gap: 16px; }

    .fadt-pill-row {
      display: flex;
      flex-wrap: wrap;
      gap: 8px;
      margin-top: 12px;
    }
    .fadt-pill {
      background: #f8fafc;
      border: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-radius: 999px;
      padding: 6px 12px;
      font-size: 0.88rem;
      color: #334155;
    }

    .fadt-banner {
      border-radius: 12px;
      padding: 12px 16px;
      font-weight: 700;
      border: 1px solid transparent;
      margin-bottom: 10px;
    }
    .fadt-banner.good { background: var(--good-bg); color: var(--good); border-color: #bbf7d0; }
    .fadt-banner.warn { background: var(--warn-bg); color: var(--warn); border-color: #fde68a; }

    .fadt-tree {
      border: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-radius: 14px;
      padding: 16px;
      background: #fbfdff;
    }

    .fadt-step {
      border-left: 4px solid var(--accent);
      background: #fff;
      border-radius: 0 12px 12px 0;
      padding: 12px 14px 12px 14px;
      margin: 10px 0;
      border-top: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-right: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
    }
    .fadt-step h3 { margin: 0 0 5px; font-size: 0.95rem; }
    .fadt-step p  { margin: 0 0 7px; font-size: 0.9rem; }
    .fadt-step ul { margin: 6px 0 0 18px; padding: 0; font-size: 0.9rem; }

    .fadt-tiny { color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.88rem; }

    .fadt-note {
      background: var(--accent-soft);
      border: 1px solid #bfdbfe;
      color: #1e3a8a;
      border-radius: 12px;
      padding: 12px 16px;
      font-size: 0.9rem;
    }

    .fadt-flow {
      display: grid;
      grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr));
      gap: 10px;
    }
    .fadt-flow-box {
      border: 1px solid var(--line);
      border-radius: 12px;
      padding: 12px;
      background: #fff;
      font-size: 0.88rem;
    }

    .fadt-footer { margin-top: 8px; color: var(--muted); font-size: 0.88rem; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
<div class="fadt-wrap">
  <div class="fadt-grid">
    <!-- Controls -->
    <div class="fadt-card">
      <h2 class="fadt-section-title">Choose your scenario</h2>

      <label for="fadt-design">Design type</label>
      <select id="fadt-design">
        <option value="mixed">Mixed ANOVA (one within, one between)</option>
        <option value="bb">Between-Between factorial ANOVA</option>
        <option value="ww">Within-Within factorial ANOVA</option>
      </select>

      <label for="fadt-interaction">Was the interaction significant?</label>
      <select id="fadt-interaction">
        <option value="yes">Yes — interaction is significant</option>
        <option value="no">No — interaction is not significant</option>
      </select>

      <label for="fadt-mainA">Main effect of Factor A</label>
      <select id="fadt-mainA">
        <option value="sig">Significant</option>
        <option value="ns">Not significant</option>
        <option value="na">Not checked yet / not needed yet</option>
      </select>

      <label for="fadt-mainB">Main effect of Factor B</label>
      <select id="fadt-mainB">
        <option value="sig">Significant</option>
        <option value="ns">Not significant</option>
        <option value="na">Not checked yet / not needed yet</option>
      </select>

      <label for="fadt-levelsA">Number of levels — Factor A</label>
      <select id="fadt-levelsA">
        <option value="2">2</option>
        <option value="3plus">3 or more</option>
      </select>

      <label for="fadt-levelsB">Number of levels — Factor B</label>
      <select id="fadt-levelsB">
        <option value="2">2</option>
        <option value="3plus">3 or more</option>
      </select>

      <div class="fadt-btn-row">
        <button class="fadt-run-btn"   id="fadt-runBtn">Show decision path</button>
        <button class="fadt-reset-btn" id="fadt-resetBtn">Reset</button>
      </div>

      <p class="fadt-helper">
        Select the design, choose whether the interaction is significant, and then review the recommended interpretation steps.
      </p>
    </div>

    <!-- Output -->
    <div class="fadt-output" id="fadt-output">
      <div class="fadt-card">
        <h2 class="fadt-section-title">Overview</h2>
        <div class="fadt-flow">
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 1</strong><br />Check assumptions for the design.</div>
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 2</strong><br />Test the interaction first.</div>
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 3</strong><br />If significant, unpack with simple effects.</div>
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 4</strong><br />If not significant, interpret main effects.</div>
        </div>
        <p class="fadt-footer">Make a selection on the left to generate a customised decision path.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  const designEl      = document.getElementById('fadt-design');
  const interactionEl = document.getElementById('fadt-interaction');
  const mainAEl       = document.getElementById('fadt-mainA');
  const mainBEl       = document.getElementById('fadt-mainB');
  const levelsAEl     = document.getElementById('fadt-levelsA');
  const levelsBEl     = document.getElementById('fadt-levelsB');
  const outputEl      = document.getElementById('fadt-output');
  const runBtn        = document.getElementById('fadt-runBtn');
  const resetBtn      = document.getElementById('fadt-resetBtn');

  const designInfo = {
    mixed: {
      title: 'Mixed ANOVA',
      summary: 'One factor is within-subjects and one factor is between-subjects.',
      assumptions: [
        'Independence of observations for the between-subject factor',
        'Approximate normality of residuals',
        'Homogeneity of variance for between-group comparisons',
        'Sphericity for the within-subject factor when it has more than 2 levels'
      ],
      interactionExample: 'A common interpretation is that groups changed differently across time.',
      apaInteraction:   'There was a significant interaction between Time and Group, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx, indicating that change over time differed across groups.',
      apaFollowUp:      'Follow-up simple effects analyses showed that the effect of Time was significant in the treatment group, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx. Adjusted pairwise comparisons indicated that posttest scores were higher than pretest scores.',
      apaNoInteraction: 'The Time × Group interaction was not significant, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx. Therefore, the main effects of Time and Group were interpreted.',
      apaMainEffect:    'There was a significant main effect of Time, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx, such that scores increased from pretest to posttest.'
    },
    bb: {
      title: 'Between-Between factorial ANOVA',
      summary: 'Both factors are between-subjects factors.',
      assumptions: [
        'Independence of observations',
        'Approximate normality of residuals',
        'Homogeneity of variance across groups'
      ],
      interactionExample: 'A common interpretation is that the effect of one grouping factor depends on the level of the other grouping factor.',
      apaInteraction:   'There was a significant interaction between Instruction Type and Sex, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx, indicating that the effect of instruction type differed by sex.',
      apaFollowUp:      'Simple effects analyses showed that Instruction Type was significant for women, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx. Tukey-adjusted comparisons indicated that the demonstration condition produced higher scores than the verbal condition.',
      apaNoInteraction: 'The interaction between Instruction Type and Sex was not significant, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx. Therefore, the main effects were interpreted.',
      apaMainEffect:    'There was a significant main effect of Instruction Type, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx, such that participants in the demonstration condition scored higher overall than participants in the verbal condition.'
    },
    ww: {
      title: 'Within-Within factorial ANOVA',
      summary: 'Both factors are repeated-measures factors.',
      assumptions: [
        'Approximate normality of residuals or difference scores',
        'Sphericity for within-subject factors with more than 2 levels',
        'Careful follow-up with paired comparisons when needed'
      ],
      interactionExample: 'A common interpretation is that the pattern of repeated responses changes across the levels of the other repeated factor.',
      apaInteraction:   'There was a significant interaction between Time and Condition, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx, indicating that change over time differed across conditions.',
      apaFollowUp:      'Follow-up repeated-measures simple effects analyses showed that the effect of Condition was significant at posttest, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx. Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons indicated that Condition 1 differed from Condition 2.',
      apaNoInteraction: 'The Time × Condition interaction was not significant, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx. Therefore, the main effects of Time and Condition were interpreted.',
      apaMainEffect:    'There was a significant main effect of Condition, <em>F</em>(df<sub>1</sub>, df<sub>2</sub>) = xx.xx, <em>p</em> = .xxx, <em>η</em><sub>p</sub><sup>2</sup> = .xx, such that scores were higher in Condition 1 than in Condition 2.'
    }
  };

  function listToHTML(items) {
    return `<ul>${items.map(i => `<li>${i}</li>`).join('')}</ul>`;
  }

  function pairwiseMsg(name, levels) {
    return levels === '3plus'
      ? `Because ${name} has <strong>3 or more levels</strong>, follow with adjusted pairwise comparisons or planned contrasts.`
      : `Because ${name} has <strong>2 levels</strong>, no post hoc pairwise test is usually needed.`;
  }

  function buildMainSection(mainA, mainB, levelsA, levelsB) {
    const blocks = [];
    if (mainA === 'sig') blocks.push(`<div class="fadt-step"><h3>Main effect of Factor A — significant</h3><p>Interpret the overall effect of Factor A across levels of Factor B.</p><p>${pairwiseMsg('Factor A', levelsA)}</p></div>`);
    else if (mainA === 'ns') blocks.push(`<div class="fadt-step"><h3>Main effect of Factor A — not significant</h3><p>Do not claim an overall effect for Factor A.</p></div>`);
    if (mainB === 'sig') blocks.push(`<div class="fadt-step"><h3>Main effect of Factor B — significant</h3><p>Interpret the overall effect of Factor B across levels of Factor A.</p><p>${pairwiseMsg('Factor B', levelsB)}</p></div>`);
    else if (mainB === 'ns') blocks.push(`<div class="fadt-step"><h3>Main effect of Factor B — not significant</h3><p>Do not claim an overall effect for Factor B.</p></div>`);
    if (mainA === 'ns' && mainB === 'ns') blocks.push(`<div class="fadt-step"><h3>Neither main effect is significant</h3><p>There is no evidence for an overall effect of Factor A or Factor B in this sample.</p></div>`);
    if (mainA === 'na' || mainB === 'na') blocks.push(`<div class="fadt-step"><h3>Main effects still need evaluation</h3><p>Check each main effect and decide whether post hoc tests are needed.</p></div>`);
    return blocks.join('');
  }

  function render() {
    const design      = designEl.value;
    const interaction = interactionEl.value;
    const mainA       = mainAEl.value;
    const mainB       = mainBEl.value;
    const levelsA     = levelsAEl.value;
    const levelsB     = levelsBEl.value;
    const info        = designInfo[design];

    const banner = interaction === 'yes'
      ? `<div class="fadt-banner warn">Interaction is significant — interpret the interaction pattern first, not the main effects.</div>`
      : `<div class="fadt-banner good">Interaction is not significant — move to the main effects.</div>`;

    const tree = interaction === 'yes' ? `
      <div class="fadt-tree">
        <div class="fadt-step">
          <h3>1. State the interaction result first</h3>
          <p>The effect of one factor depends on the level of the other factor.</p>
          <p class="fadt-tiny">${info.interactionExample}</p>
        </div>
        <div class="fadt-step">
          <h3>2. Run simple effects (or simple main effects)</h3>
          <p>Examine one factor at each level of the other to find where the differences occur.</p>
          <ul>
            <li>Apply a multiplicity correction (e.g., Bonferroni)</li>
            <li>Run pairwise comparisons within each simple effect if that factor has 3+ levels</li>
          </ul>
        </div>
        <div class="fadt-step">
          <h3>3. Pairwise guidance based on your factor levels</h3>
          <p>${pairwiseMsg('Factor A within each level of Factor B', levelsA)}</p>
          <p>${pairwiseMsg('Factor B within each level of Factor A', levelsB)}</p>
        </div>
        <div class="fadt-step">
          <h3>4. Report main effects as context only</h3>
          <p>Main effects may be mentioned but should not be the headline result — they can obscure the interaction pattern.</p>
        </div>
      </div>` : `
      <div class="fadt-tree">
        <div class="fadt-step">
          <h3>1. State that the interaction is not significant</h3>
          <p>There is no strong evidence that the effect of one factor depends on the level of the other factor.</p>
        </div>
        <div class="fadt-step">
          <h3>2. Evaluate each main effect</h3>
          <p>Interpret the overall effect of Factor A and the overall effect of Factor B independently.</p>
        </div>
        ${buildMainSection(mainA, mainB, levelsA, levelsB)}
        <div class="fadt-step">
          <h3>3. Use post hoc tests only when needed</h3>
          <p>Post hoc tests are needed only for factors with 3+ levels and a significant main effect.</p>
        </div>
      </div>`;

    const apaBlock = interaction === 'yes'
      ? `<p><strong>Interaction:</strong> ${info.apaInteraction}</p><p><strong>Follow-up:</strong> ${info.apaFollowUp}</p>`
      : `<p><strong>Interaction (ns):</strong> ${info.apaNoInteraction}</p><p><strong>Main effect:</strong> ${info.apaMainEffect}</p>`;

    outputEl.innerHTML = `
      <div class="fadt-card">
        <h2 class="fadt-section-title">Your decision path</h2>
        ${banner}
        <div class="fadt-pill-row">
          <div class="fadt-pill"><strong>Design:</strong> ${info.title}</div>
          <div class="fadt-pill">${info.summary}</div>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="fadt-card">
        <h2 class="fadt-section-title">Design-specific assumptions</h2>
        ${listToHTML(info.assumptions)}
        <p class="fadt-tiny">If a within-subject factor has more than 2 levels, check sphericity (Mauchly's test) and apply Greenhouse-Geisser or Huynh-Feldt correction if needed.</p>
      </div>

      <div class="fadt-card">
        <h2 class="fadt-section-title">Decision path</h2>
        ${tree}
      </div>

      <div class="fadt-card">
        <h2 class="fadt-section-title">APA-style reporting examples</h2>
        ${apaBlock}
        <div class="fadt-note" style="margin-top:12px;">
          <strong>APA reminders:</strong> Report the effect first, then <em>F</em>, degrees of freedom in parentheses, the exact <em>p</em> value, and an effect size (e.g., η²<sub>p</sub>). For <em>p</em> &lt; .001, write <em>p</em> &lt; .001. Italicise statistical symbols (<em>F</em>, <em>p</em>, <em>M</em>, <em>SD</em>).
        </div>
      </div>

      <div class="fadt-card">
        <h2 class="fadt-section-title">References</h2>
        <p style="font-size:0.88rem;">American Psychological Association. (2024). <em>APA Style numbers and statistics guide</em>. https://apastyle.apa.org/instructional-aids/numbers-statistics-guide.pdf</p>
        <p style="font-size:0.88rem;">Pennsylvania State University, Department of Statistics. (n.d.). <em>Lesson 5: Introduction to factorial designs</em> (STAT 503). https://online.stat.psu.edu/stat503/lesson/5</p>
        <p style="font-size:0.88rem;">UCLA IDRE Statistical Consulting Group. (n.d.). <em>How can I test simple effects in repeated measures models?</em> https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/faq/how-can-i-test-simple-effects-in-repeated-measures-models-stata-12/</p>
      </div>
    `;
  }

  function reset() {
    designEl.value = 'mixed'; interactionEl.value = 'yes';
    mainAEl.value = 'sig'; mainBEl.value = 'sig';
    levelsAEl.value = '2'; levelsBEl.value = '2';
    outputEl.innerHTML = `
      <div class="fadt-card">
        <h2 class="fadt-section-title">Overview</h2>
        <div class="fadt-flow">
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 1</strong><br />Check assumptions for the design.</div>
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 2</strong><br />Test the interaction first.</div>
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 3</strong><br />If significant, unpack with simple effects.</div>
          <div class="fadt-flow-box"><strong>Step 4</strong><br />If not significant, interpret main effects.</div>
        </div>
        <p class="fadt-footer">Make a selection on the left to generate a customised decision path.</p>
      </div>`;
  }

  runBtn.addEventListener('click', render);
  resetBtn.addEventListener('click', reset);
})();
</script>
</body>
</html>
```
